'''Barrie Ciliberti''' (born July 27, 1936) is an American professor and politician. He is a professor at the [[University of Maryland University College]] and current [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] legislator in the [[Maryland House of Delegates]], representing [[Maryland Legislative District 4|District 4]]. He previously represented [[Maryland Legislative District 39|District 39]] in the House of Delegates from 1995 to 1999.

==Early life and education==
Ciliberti was born in [[Philadelphia, Pennsylvania]], where he graduated from [[Friends Select School]]. He later attended [[Ursinus College]], where he earned a [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] degree in history in 1957; [[Georgetown University]], where he earned a [[Master of Arts|M.A.]] degree in history in 1960; and [[Catholic University of America|Catholic University]], where he earned a [[Ph.D.]] degree in administration in 1975.<ref name="msa-maryland-gov">{{cite web |title=Barrie S. Ciliberti, Maryland State Delegate |url=https://msa.maryland.gov/msa/mdmanual/06hse/html/msa12199.html |website=Maryland Manual On-Line |publisher=Maryland State Archives |access-date=February 25, 2025}}</ref>

Ciliberti is married to his wife, Pam, and has five adult children.<ref name="msa-maryland-gov" /> Outside of politics, he enjoys [[Mountaineering|mountain climbing]] and spending time with his children. His family moved from [[Rockville, Maryland|Rockville]] to [[Urbana, Maryland|Urbana]] in the early 2000s.<ref name="Beyond">{{cite news |last1=Masters |first1=Kate |title=Beyond the Ballot — Del. Barrie Ciliberti |url=https://www.fredericknewspost.com/news/politics_and_government/levels_of_government/state/delegates/beyond-the-ballot-del-barrie-ciliberti/article_b407fba7-abed-5940-a2ff-fc6df569764f.html |access-date=April 25, 2022 |work=[[The Frederick News-Post]] |date=January 30, 2019}}</ref>

==Career==
Since 1965, Ciliberti has worked as an associate professor of education at [[Bowie State University]].<ref name="msa-maryland-gov" /><ref>{{cite web |title=Bowie State University Graduate School Catalog 2016 – 2018 |url=https://bowiestate.edu/academics/2016-2018-graduate-catalog.pdf |website=bowiestate.edu |publisher=[[Bowie State University]] |access-date=April 25, 2022}}</ref>

In 1985, Ciliberti was appointed by President [[Ronald Reagan]] to a member of the National Graduate Fellows Program Fellowship Board for a six-year term.<ref>{{Cite web|date=13 September 1985|title=Nomination of Paul Freedenberg To Be an Assistant Secretary of Commerce|url=https://reaganlibrary.archives.gov/archives/speeches/1985/91385d.htm|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160408125340/https://reaganlibrary.archives.gov/archives/speeches/1985/91385d.htm|archive-date=8 April 2016}}</ref> President Reagan also appointed Dr Ciliberti to serve as a member of the National Advisory Council on Adult Education. He has served as a guest lecturer for the [[U.S. Information Agency]] and a special assistant for ethnic affairs with the [[Republican National Committee]].<ref name="msa-maryland-gov" />

In 1994, Ciliberti was elected to the Maryland House of Delegates in District 39, riding the [[Republican Revolution|Gingrich wave]] to victory. He lost re-election to a second term in 1998, losing to Democrats [[Charles E. Barkley|Charles Barkley]], [[Paul Carlson (politician)|Paul Carlson]], and [[Joan F. Stern]].<ref name="Bourbon">{{cite news |last1=Kurtz |first1=Josh |title=Del. Barrie Ciliberti wishes a Democrat would offer him a bourbon and branch |url=https://www.marylandmatters.org/2017/04/03/del-barrie-ciliberti-wishes-a-democrat-would-offer-him-a-bourbon-and-branch/ |access-date=April 25, 2022 |work=[[Maryland Matters]] |date=April 3, 2017}}</ref>

Ciliberti unsuccessfully ran for Congress in [[1996 United States House of Representatives elections in Maryland|1996]], losing to incumbent [[U.S. Representative]] [[Connie Morella]] in the Republican primary election.<ref name="Bourbon"/>

Dr. Ciliberti has served two civilian tours in [[Iraq]] working with the United States Department of State.  On his first term, he worked with the United States Embassy in [[Baghdad]] on election security in advance of the [[January 2005 Iraqi parliamentary election|historic elections in Iraq on January 30, 2005]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Buck|first=Tara|date=March 13, 2005|title=Urbana man witnesses Iraq's historic elections|url=http://www.fredericknewspost.com/sections/archives/display_detail.htm?StoryID=49493|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121012171744/http://www.fredericknewspost.com/sections/archives/display_detail.htm?StoryID=49493|archive-date=October 12, 2012}}</ref> Dr. Ciliberti's second tour was 255 miles north of Baghdad in the city of Mosul, Iraq where he served as the Senior Governance Advisor for Ninewah Province where he helped build the governance capacity of Provincial and city leaders throughout [[Nineveh Governorate|Ninewah Province]].{{citation needed|date=April 2022}}

In 2014, Ciliberti unsuccessfully ran for the Maryland House of Delegates in District 4, receiving 14.0 percent of the vote in the Republican primary.<ref name="2014p" />

In January 2015, the Frederick County Republican Central Committee recommended Ciliberti to replace [[Kelly Schulz]] in the Maryland House of Delegates after she was appointed to serve in Governor-elect [[Larry Hogan]]'s cabinet as the [[Maryland Department of Labor|Secretary of Labor]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hayes |first1=Wiley |title=Frederick committee recommends Ciliberti for District 4 |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2015/01/08/frederick-committee-recommends-ciliberti-for-district-4/ |access-date=April 25, 2022 |work=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |date=January 8, 2015}}</ref> The Carroll County Republican Central Committee also voted to recommend Ciliberti, in addition to Jason Miller and Ken Timmerman, to fill the vacancy.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hayes |first1=Wiley |title=Hogan to request multiple names from committees; Carroll committee votes to offer 3 for District 4 |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2015/01/23/hogan-to-request-multiple-names-from-committees-carroll-committee-votes-to-offer-3-for-district-4/ |access-date=April 25, 2022 |work=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |agency=[[Carroll County Times]] |date=January 23, 2015}}</ref> Hogan appointed Ciliberti to the House of Delegates on February 3, 2015.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hayes |first1=Wiley |title=Hogan decides delegate vacancy to be filled by Ciliberti |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2015/02/03/hogan-decides-delegate-vacancy-to-be-filled-by-ciliberti/ |access-date=April 25, 2022 |work=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |agency=[[Carroll County Times]] |date=February 3, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Rodgers |first1=Bethany |title=Ciliberti says Hogan picks him to fill District 4 delegate seat |url=https://www.fredericknewspost.com/news/ciliberti-says-hogan-picks-him-to-fill-district-4-delegate-seat/article_3bc42b9f-789c-57a4-a997-52c347966cc8.html |access-date=April 25, 2022 |work=[[The Frederick News-Post]] |date=February 3, 2015}}</ref>

==In the legislature==
Ciliberti was sworn into the Maryland House of Delegates to represent District 39 on January 11, 1995.<ref name="msa-maryland-gov" /> During his legislative career in the Maryland General Assembly, he became known for his opposition to mandatory [[volunteerism]]<ref>{{Cite magazine|last=Cloud|first=John|date=1 December 1997|title=Involuntary Volunteers|url=http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,987444,00.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071001002712/http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,987444,00.html|archive-date=1 October 2007|magazine=Time}}</ref> and his stance against aggressive driving.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2004-08-21|title=Can Aggressive Driving be Curbed?|url=http://www.ncsl.org/programs/transportation/transer7.htm|archive-url=https://archive.today/20040821080505/http://www.ncsl.org/programs/transportation/transer7.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=2004-08-21|access-date=2020-08-25|website=archive.is}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Valentine |first1=Paul W. |title=THOUSANDS CITED IN AGGRESSIVE-DRIVING CRACKDOWN |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/local/1997/05/17/thousands-cited-in-aggressive-driving-crackdown/a7d44826-43d6-4b80-9693-9d030f026a88/ |access-date=April 26, 2022 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=May 17, 1997}}</ref> He was a member of the Environmental Matters Committee.<ref name="msa-maryland-gov"/>

Ciliberti was again sworn into the Maryland House of Delegates to represent District 4 on February 4, 2015 after paying campaign finance infractions for missing campaign finance reports.<ref name="msa-maryland-gov" /><ref>{{cite news |last1=Rodgers |first1=Bethany |title=Ciliberti takes office as delegate after paying campaign fines |url=https://www.fredericknewspost.com/news/politics_and_government/elections/ciliberti-takes-office-as-delegate-after-paying-campaign-fines/article_148ddfd8-b5ea-5391-b3f5-b8a062bc2bbb.html |access-date=April 25, 2022 |work=[[The Frederick News-Post]] |date=February 5, 2015}}</ref> He was a member of the Appropriations Committee from 2015 to 2018, afterwards serving on the Environment and Transportation Committee until 2025. During the 2026 legislative session, Ciliberti was a member of the Government, Labor, and Elections Committee.<ref name="msa-maryland-gov"/>

Ciliberti was an early and enthusiastic supporter of [[Donald Trump]], even when many in the [[Maryland Republican Party]] were keeping their distance.<ref name="Bourbon"/> In 2016, Ciliberti ran to be a delegate to the [[2016 Republican National Convention|Republican National Convention]], pledged to Trump. He won the Republican primary with 15.4 percent of the vote.<ref name="2016p"/> He ran again as an alternate delegate pledged to Trump in [[2020 Republican National Convention|2020]], receiving 32.8 percent of the vote in the Republican primary.<ref name="2020p"/>

==Political positions==
===Abortion===
Ciliberti supports the overturning of ''[[Roe v. Wade]]'', saying that the issue of abortion should be left to the states.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Arias |first1=Jeremy |title=Activists in Frederick join nationwide reproductive rights protest |url=https://www.fredericknewspost.com/news/politics_and_government/activists-in-frederick-join-nationwide-reproductive-rights-protest/article_f6524d36-3dec-5b40-9912-ca393991519c.html |access-date=April 26, 2022 |work=[[The Frederick News-Post]] |date=May 21, 2019}}</ref>

During the 2015 legislative session, Ciliberti introduced legislation that would prohibit abortions past 20 weeks, excluding specific medical emergencies.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hayes |first1=Wiley |title=Carroll legislators attempt to amend abortion law |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2015/03/06/carroll-legislators-attempt-to-amend-abortion-law/ |access-date=April 25, 2022 |work=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |agency=[[Carroll County Times]] |date=March 6, 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Legislation - HB0961 |url=https://mgaleg.maryland.gov/mgawebsite/Legislation/Details/hb0961?ys=2015RS |website=mgaleg.maryland.gov |publisher=[[Maryland General Assembly]] |access-date=April 25, 2022}}</ref> The bill was re-introduced during the 2016 legislative session.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Norris |first1=Heather |title=Local legislators sponsor bill limiting time span for abortion |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2016/02/14/local-legislators-sponsor-bill-limiting-time-span-for-abortion/ |access-date=April 25, 2022 |work=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |agency=[[Carroll County Times]] |date=February 14, 2016}}</ref>

In September 2015, Ciliberti and state Senator [[Michael Hough (politician)|Michael Hough]] wrote a letter to [[David R. Brinkley|David Brinkley]], the Maryland Secretary of Budget and Management, to push the state to eliminate funding for [[Planned Parenthood]] from the state's budget.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Cox |first1=Erin |last2=Wenger |first2=Yvonne |title=Lawmakers pressure Hogan on Planned Parenthood funding |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2015/09/29/lawmakers-pressure-hogan-on-planned-parenthood-funding/ |access-date=April 25, 2022 |work=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |date=September 29, 2015}}</ref>

During the 2024 legislative session, Ciliberti introduced a bill that would require a 24-hour waiting period after a pregnant person receives a [[transabdominal ultrasound]] before a provider could perform an abortion.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ford |first1=William J. |last2=Kurtz |first2=Josh |last3=Brown |first3=Danielle J. |title=Legislative notes: Some highlights from a busy day in Annapolis |url=https://www.marylandmatters.org/2024/03/16/legislative-notes-some-highlights-from-a-busy-day-in-annapolis/ |access-date=March 16, 2024 |work=[[Maryland Matters]] |date=March 16, 2024}}</ref>

===Business===
In July 2015, the Maryland Business for Responsible Government gave Ciliberti a score of 86 percent in its annual legislative scorecard.<ref name="MBRG2015">{{cite news |last1=Hayes |first1=Wiley |title=Separate reports find Carroll legislators support business initiatives over environmental ones |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2015/07/25/separate-reports-find-carroll-legislators-support-business-initiatives-over-environmental-ones/ |access-date=April 25, 2022 |work=[[The Baltimore Sun]] |agency=[[Carroll County Times]] |date=July 25, 2015}}</ref>

===COVID-19 pandemic===
Ciliberti introduced legislation in the 2020 legislative session that would charge people who attack doctors or nurses with a sentence of up to 10 years in prison, a $5,000 fine, or both.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Bohnel |first1=Steve |title=Del. Ciliberti calls on lawmakers to examine emergency worker protections |url=https://www.fredericknewspost.com/news/continuing_coverage/annapolis_coverage/del-ciliberti-calls-on-lawmakers-to-examine-emergency-worker-protections/article_53750fb8-5e7e-53b6-a54a-2c860dc81cb1.html |access-date=April 25, 2022 |work=[[The Frederick News-Post]] |date=April 25, 2022}}</ref>

In April 2020, Ciliberti questioned the legality of the [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|mask mandates]] implemented by an executive order issued by Governor Hogan, calling the mandates "draconian".<ref>{{cite news |last1=DePuyt |first1=Bruce |title=GOP Lawmakers From Rural Areas Want Hogan to Ease Restrictions |url=https://www.marylandmatters.org/2020/04/16/gop-lawmakers-from-rural-areas-want-hogan-to-ease-restrictions/ |access-date=April 25, 2022 |work=[[Maryland Matters]] |date=April 16, 2020}}</ref>

===Education===
In April 2019, Ciliberti voted against the [[Blueprint for Maryland's Future]]. He was the only member of the Frederick County delegation to do so.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hogan |first1=Samantha |title=General Assembly approves first phase of sweeping education reform |url=https://www.fredericknewspost.com/news/education/funding/general-assembly-approves-first-phase-of-sweeping-education-reform/article_d3ce3efd-020c-52bf-a28c-3374296c6e0a.html |access-date=April 26, 2022 |work=[[The Frederick News-Post]] |date=April 8, 2019}}</ref>

===Environment===
In July 2015, the Maryland Business for Responsible Government gave Ciliberti a score of 50 percent in its annual legislative scorecard.<ref name="MBRG2015" />

In April 2021, Ciliberti joined Democrats in the House Environment and Transportation Committee in voting in favor of the Climate Solutions Now Act of 2021.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Shwe |first1=Elizabeth |title=Md. House Panels Move Climate Bill as Pinsky Tries to Find Other Vehicles For His Priorities |url=https://www.marylandmatters.org/2021/04/09/md-house-panels-move-climate-bill-as-pinsky-tries-to-find-other-vehicles-for-his-priorities/ |access-date=April 25, 2022 |work=[[Maryland Matters]] |date=April 9, 2021}}</ref>

===Guns===
In March 2018, Ciliberti voted against a bill that would ban [[bump stock]]s, which passed the Maryland House of Delegates by a vote of 128-7. He was the only member of the Frederick County delegation to vote against the bill.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Loos |first1=Kelsi |title=Bump stock ban bill passes Maryland House |url=https://www.fredericknewspost.com/news/politics_and_government/bump-stock-ban-bill-passes-maryland-house/article_2f327b9a-e895-54c1-a8ec-43a8ac6fc251.html |access-date=April 26, 2022 |work=[[The Frederick News-Post]] |date=March 15, 2018}}</ref>

===National politics===
In December 2019, Ciliberti called the [[first impeachment of Donald Trump]] an "attempted [[Coup d'état|coup d'etat]]".<ref>{{cite news |last1=Bohnel |first1=Steve |last2=Marshall |first2=Ryan |title=Much like Congress, local leaders split along party lines on Trump impeachment |url=https://www.fredericknewspost.com/news/politics_and_government/levels_of_government/federal/house/much-like-congress-local-leaders-split-along-party-lines-on-trump-impeachment/article_ee73365c-6d2a-5dda-b2bb-0ae978d98711.html |access-date=April 26, 2022 |work=[[The Frederick News-Post]] |date=December 18, 2019}}</ref>
